introduction.what: This gentle scramble method stirs beaten eggs into small, soft, creamy curds.
introduction.why: It teaches you to respond to texture by stirring and moving the pan away from excess heat.

quiz.question: Which texture is the aim of this scramble method?
How do you stir the eggs for this gentle scramble?
choices: Only across the surface, leaving the base untouched.
Continuously, scraping the bottom and corners.
Only after a browned layer has formed.

quiz.question: Which spoon trail matches the texture described here?
choices: A dry gap that never closes.
No trail in a completely watery mixture.

quiz.question: The curds are forming too fast. What would you do?
choices: Lift the pan off the heat and keep stirring.
Keep the pan on the heat and stir faster.
Reduce stirring so the curds have time to join together.
